chunks.arabic_text: رِجَالُ الْكَشِّيِّ: مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ مَسْعُودٍ، عَنْ عَلِيِّ بْنِ الْحُسَيْنِ، عَنْ عَلِيِّ بْنِ فَضَالٍ، عَنِ الْعَبَّاسِ بْنِ عَامِرٍ، عَنْ أَبَانَ بْنِ عُثْمَانَ، عَنِ الشَّهَابِ بْنِ عَبْدِ رَبِّهِ قَالَ

translations.en: Rijal al-Kashshi: Muhammad ibn Mas'ud, from Ali ibn al-Hasan, from Ali ibn Fadhal, from al-Abbas ibn 'Amir, from Aban ibn Uthman, from al-Shihab ibn 'Abd Rabbah who said:

chunks.arabic_text: قُلْتُ لِأَبِي عَبْدِ اللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ السَّلَامُ: كَيْفَ أَصْبَحْتَ؟ جَعَلْتُكَ فَدَايَ؟ قَالَ: أَصْبَحْتُ أَقُولُ: كَمَا قَالَ أَبُو الطُّفَيْلِ عَامِرُ بْنُ وَاثِلَةَ: وَإِنَّ لِأَهْلِ الْحَقِّ لَبَدَ دَوْلَةً *** عَلَى النَّاسِ إِيَّاهَا أَرْجُو وَأَرْقُبُ. قَالَ: أَنَا وَ اللَّهِ مِنْهُمُ يُرْجَى وَيُرْقَبُ.

translations.en: I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): How did you feel this morning? May I be your ransom. He said: I woke up saying: As Abu al-Tufayl 'Amir ibn Wathila said: 'And surely for the People of Truth there must be a period of rule over the people, for which I am hopeful and constantly waiting.' He said: By Allah, I am one of those who are hoped for and waited for.

en.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) affirms his status as a leader of the 'People of Truth' by quoting the poet Abu al-Tufayl 'Amir ibn Wathila, thereby connecting the historical expectation of divine victory with the living presence of the Imams. This narration underscores the Shia doctrine of *al-Dawla* (the eventual rise of the righteous), where the Imam himself embodies the hope and anticipation of the faithful for the establishment of justice. The reference highlights the continuity between the prophetic tradition and the Imams' role as the active agents of this promised divine state.
en.seo_question: What did Imam al-Sadiq say about the rise of the People of Truth?
